title: SpeechOcean762
citation: Zhang, Junbo et al. SpeechOcean762: An Open-Source Non-native English Speech Corpus for Pronunciation Assessment. Interspeech 2021.

licence.attribution_text: Cite Zhang et al., SpeechOcean762, Interspeech 2021, and retain CC BY 4.0 attribution.

governance.retention_or_deletion_duties: Retain privately only while needed, preserve attribution, and never commit raw audio or participant metadata.

population.description: Five thousand read English utterances from 250 Mandarin first language speakers, split evenly between the source child and adult populations.
limitations: The population is not representative of all English speakers or Australian English.
The source rubric uses a single expected pronunciation and includes accent and native likeness judgements that this project rejects.

annotation.provenance: Five experts scored independently. scores-detail.json retains each reviewer phone string and disagreement.
limitations: Curly brace score one means right with heavy accent and is not imported as an error.
Parentheses combine incorrect and missed phones, so unresolved cases remain uncertain.
The aggregated mispronunciations block is supporting evidence only and does not replace five original reviewer records.

inspected_materials: All 5,000 scores-detail.json records checked for five reviewer vectors.
findings: All 250 speakers are exclusive across the original train and test sets.
All 5,000 utterances retain five top level and five per word reviewer records.
Explicit insertion, zero or missed, and accent marked notation exists.
Scalar pronunciation and accent scores are excluded from phone relation truth.

participant_split.source_split_provenance: Original train and test membership retained privately; original speaker overlap is zero.
participant_split.project_strategy: Stable SHA256 order within source child or adult and gender strata, then exact 60 percent development, 20 percent tuning and 20 percent held out.

lineage.duplicate_detection: Private participant and utterance ids are checked before every benchmark assembly.
